items.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Replace the reference scene, keeping its black ink crosshatched literary illustration style on white paper, landscape 3:2. Two clearly separated sequential panels with white gutter and thin frame, no lettering. SAME recognizable moustached ordinary adult with wavy hair and rolled-sleeve plain shirt in both panels. LEFT he claps his empty hands, distracting two seated diners beside a plate of khichdi (soft rice lentil mixture). RIGHT, a moment later, he runs away carrying that same food plate securely with both hands while the same diners look surprised behind him. The clapper and food-taker are ONE person shown at different times, never two accomplices. Believable anatomy, hands, grips and motion. No caste or religious identifiers. Preserve natural linework and generous white space, simplify background. No words, labels, arrows or watermarks.

Use case: illustration-story. Recompose reference into TWO clearly separated sequential panels with a white gutter and fine border, landscape 3:2, black ink and pencil crosshatching on white matching reference. SAME curly-haired short-bearded ordinary man wearing same plain rolled-sleeve shirt, SAME meeting table and chair in both panels. LEFT: he boasts expansively with raised open hand and confident expression to a quiet colleague. RIGHT: the very same man is hunched low in his chair, head lowered, hands clasped timidly after an imposing older visitor with glasses and a plain vest enters the doorway. The visitor is an imagined modern application, no insignia, political or religious symbols. Make facial identity and clothing unmistakably consistent across panels; do not show two copies in a single scene. Natural hand anatomy, clear contrast between boast and fear, selective detail. No text or labels.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the reference, preserving both people, their poses, faces, clothes, doorway, black-and-white pen crosshatching and overall landscape composition. Replace ONLY the broken deep round mortar and its pestle in the foreground with a broken FLAT BROAD RECTANGULAR STONE GRINDING SLAB, low profile approximately 4cm thick, with a flat slightly worn upper grinding surface and a large visible through-crack separating two flat pieces. Add a separate horizontal cylindrical stone grinding ROLLER lying next to the slab, with rounded ends. Small flat stone fragments near the crack. Absolutely NO bowl, basin, cavity, deep mortar or upright pestle. Ground contact, scale and perspective must be plausible. This is the rueful aftermath of displaced anger, no active violence. No text. Preserve 3:2 landscape.

Use case: illustration-story. Use reference ONLY for black-and-white literary pen/pencil crosshatching style; replace scene completely. Landscape 3:2 on white paper. An ordinary adult in a loose plain shirt and trousers, no caste or religious identifiers, has eaten an exaggerated large meal and is now just beginning to rise beside a very low wooden stool whose flat wooden seat has a clearly visible crack. One hand rests on his full covered belly, other hand steadies on knee as he rises, expression mildly overfull not distressed. A used meal plate and two mostly empty serving bowls nearby convey the finished meal. Natural proportions, no obesity caricature, no bare belly, no mocking audience or person commanding him to rise. The moment means only then does he get up after eating too much. Clear stool crack and believable joints, weight and hand anatomy. Sparse home backdrop, white space, restrained gentle humor. No text or labels.

Use case: illustration-story. Use reference as style and character reference. Black-white pen/pencil crosshatching, landscape 3:2. TWO clearly separated sequential panels with white gutter and thin frame. SAME older moustached craftworker with glasses and rolled-sleeve shirt in both. LEFT: when his coin pouch is full, he eagerly hands several coins to a seller for an unnecessary decorative vase; two similar decorative purchases already sit beside him. RIGHT: later in his small workshop, he holds the same pouch upside down, clearly empty, worried beside unfinished wooden work and an empty supply shelf. The three decorative purchases are still visible to connect the wasteful spending to later lack of necessary materials. Distinct concrete action of spending first and shortage later. Natural gestures and hands, no generic poverty tableau. Do not crowd every surface. No text, currency numerals, labels, brands or symbols. Preserve reference linework and generous white background.
